content: Studies have demonstrated that Opuntia ficus-indica may exhibit hypoglycemic effects in patients with Type 2 diabetes. However, there is insufficient evidence to support its use for managing benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), and further research is required. Opuntia ficus-indica has been shown to enhance the effects of various antidiabetic medications through pharmacodynamic synergism. These medications include acarbose, glimepiride, glipizide, glyburide, insulin aspart, insulin detemir, insulin glargine, insulin glulisine, insulin lispro, insulin NPH, regular human insulin, metformin, miglitol, nateglinide, pioglitazone, repaglinide, rosiglitazone, saxagliptin, sitagliptin, and vildagliptin. Due to this interaction, it is recommended to use caution and closely monitor patients when Opuntia ficus-indica is co-administered with these agents to avoid potential hypoglycemia or other adverse effects. Regarding pregnancy and lactation, there is no significant evidence to suggest that Opuntia ficus-indica poses a risk during pregnancy, particularly when using the roots. However, its effectiveness may be reduced when consumed with high-fiber foods. The pregnancy category for Opuntia ficus-indica is not assigned (NA), and its safety during lactation remains unknown. Controlled studies in pregnant women have not shown evidence of fetal risk, suggesting that it may generally be acceptable for use during pregnancy. However, caution is advised, and consultation with a healthcare provider is recommended.
